children.text: A silver nanoparticle of radius \(R=10.0\,\mathrm{nm}\) has one free electron per silver atom. Its positive ion sphere is fixed. Model its electrons as a uniformly charged sphere which can shift by \(x_p\ll R\) along \(x\). All relative permittivities are one. Use \(\rho_{Ag}=1.049\times10^4\,\mathrm{kg/m^3}\), molar mass \(M_{Ag}=0.1079\,\mathrm{kg/mol}\), \(N_A=6.022\times10^{23}\,\mathrm{mol^{-1}}\), \(e=1.602\times10^{-19}\,\mathrm C\), \(m_e=9.109\times10^{-31}\,\mathrm{kg}\), \(\epsilon_0=8.854\times10^{-12}\,\mathrm{F/m}\), and \(c=2.998\times10^8\,\mathrm{m/s}\). Electron charge is \(-e\).

nodes.alt: Original five-panel silver nanoparticle and vessel model showing the displaced charge distributions, external field and illumination geometry.

children.text: Find particle volume and mass, ion number and charge density, electron concentration \(n\), total electron charge \(Q\), and total electron mass \(m_0\).

Create a spherical neutral cavity inside a uniformly charged sphere of density \(\rho\) by adding a smaller sphere of density \(-\rho\), centred at \(\mathbf x_d\). Prove the cavity field is uniform, \(\mathbf E=A(\rho/\epsilon_0)\mathbf x_d\), and find \(A\).
Find the restoring force and work for displacing the electron cloud by \(x_p\), using \(n,R,e,\epsilon_0\).
Apply \(\mathbf E_0=-E_0\hat{\mathbf x}\). Find \(x_p\) and the electron charge \(-\Delta Q\) transported through the central yz-plane.
Match \(W_{el}=\Delta Q^2/(2C)\). Find \(C\) and its numerical value.
Find the equivalent applied voltage \(V_0\) in terms of \(R,E_0\).
If the electron cloud moves at velocity \(v\hat{\mathbf x}\), find its kinetic energy and conventional current through the yz-plane.
Find the LC resonance angular frequency.
Find the resonance angular frequency and vacuum wavelength.

An oscillating field drives cloud velocity \(v\). Each electron loses all its kinetic energy in a collision, with mean collision interval \(\tau=5.24\times10^{-15}\,\mathrm s\gg1/\omega_p\). Find average Joule power and mean-square current explicitly in terms of \(\langle v^2\rangle\).
Find and evaluate the equivalent resistance for collision heating.
The scattered power is \(P_{scat}=Q^2x_0^2\omega_p^4/(12\pi\epsilon_0c^3)\). Find \(R_{scat}=P_{scat}/\langle I^2\rangle\) and its numerical value.
The equivalent LCR series circuit is driven by \(V=V_0\cos\omega_pt\). Derive both mean power losses in terms of \(E_0\).

The particle concentration is \(n_{np}=7.3\times10^{15}\,\mathrm{m^{-3}}\) in a vessel \(h\times h\times a=10\times10\times1.0\,\mathrm{cm^3}\). Light enters through area \(h^2\) at the same intensity. All nanoparticle Joule heating converts water at \(20^\circ\mathrm C\) to steam at \(100^\circ\mathrm C\), without heating bulk water. Use \(c_w=4.181\times10^3\,\mathrm{J/(kg\,K)}\) and \(L_w=2.260\times10^6\,\mathrm{J/kg}\). Find steam mass per second.

statement.text:
Plasmonic Steam Generator
A silver nanoparticle of radius \(R=10.0\,\mathrm{nm}\) has one free electron per silver atom. Its positive ion sphere is fixed. Model its electrons as a uniformly charged sphere which can shift by \(x_p\ll R\) along \(x\). All relative permittivities are one. Use \(\rho_{Ag}=1.049\times10^4\,\mathrm{kg/m^3}\), molar mass \(M_{Ag}=0.1079\,\mathrm{kg/mol}\), \(N_A=6.022\times10^{23}\,\mathrm{mol^{-1}}\), \(e=1.602\times10^{-19}\,\mathrm C\), \(m_e=9.109\times10^{-31}\,\mathrm{kg}\), \(\epsilon_0=8.854\times10^{-12}\,\mathrm{F/m}\), and \(c=2.998\times10^8\,\mathrm{m/s}\). Electron charge is \(-e\).

2.1. Particle and electron properties
Find particle volume and mass, ion number and charge density, electron concentration \(n\), total electron charge \(Q\), and total electron mass \(m_0\).
2.2. Neutral cavity field
Create a spherical neutral cavity inside a uniformly charged sphere of density \(\rho\) by adding a smaller sphere of density \(-\rho\), centred at \(\mathbf x_d\). Prove the cavity field is uniform, \(\mathbf E=A(\rho/\epsilon_0)\mathbf x_d\), and find \(A\).
2.3. Restoring force and work
Find the restoring force and work for displacing the electron cloud by \(x_p\), using \(n,R,e,\epsilon_0\).
2.4. Static displacement and separated charge
Apply \(\mathbf E_0=-E_0\hat{\mathbf x}\). Find \(x_p\) and the electron charge \(-\Delta Q\) transported through the central yz-plane.
2.5a. Equivalent capacitance
Match \(W_{el}=\Delta Q^2/(2C)\). Find \(C\) and its numerical value.
2.5b. Equivalent voltage
Find the equivalent applied voltage \(V_0\) in terms of \(R,E_0\).
2.6a. Kinetic energy and current
If the electron cloud moves at velocity \(v\hat{\mathbf x}\), find its kinetic energy and conventional current through the yz-plane.
2.6b. Equivalent inductance
Use \(W_{kin}=LI^2/2\) to find and evaluate \(L\).
2.7a. Plasmon angular frequency
Find the LC resonance angular frequency.
2.7b. Resonance values
Find the resonance angular frequency and vacuum wavelength.
2.8a. Collision heating
An oscillating field drives cloud velocity \(v\). Each electron loses all its kinetic energy in a collision, with mean collision interval \(\tau=5.24\times10^{-15}\,\mathrm s\gg1/\omega_p\). Find average Joule power and mean-square current explicitly in terms of \(\langle v^2\rangle\).
2.8b. Heating resistance
Find and evaluate the equivalent resistance for collision heating.
2.9. Scattering resistance
The scattered power is \(P_{scat}=Q^2x_0^2\omega_p^4/(12\pi\epsilon_0c^3)\). Find \(R_{scat}=P_{scat}/\langle I^2\rangle\) and its numerical value.
2.10a. Resonant absorbed and scattered power
The equivalent LCR series circuit is driven by \(V=V_0\cos\omega_pt\). Derive both mean power losses in terms of \(E_0\).
2.10b. Illumination values
Use incident intensity \(S=\epsilon_0cE_0^2/2=1.00\,\mathrm{MW/m^2}\). Evaluate \(E_0,P_{heat},P_{scat}\).
2.11a. Steam mass rate
The particle concentration is \(n_{np}=7.3\times10^{15}\,\mathrm{m^{-3}}\) in a vessel \(h\times h\times a=10\times10\times1.0\,\mathrm{cm^3}\). Light enters through area \(h^2\) at the same intensity. All nanoparticle Joule heating converts water at \(20^\circ\mathrm C\) to steam at \(100^\circ\mathrm C\), without heating bulk water. Use \(c_w=4.181\times10^3\,\mathrm{J/(kg\,K)}\) and \(L_w=2.260\times10^6\,\mathrm{J/kg}\). Find steam mass per second.
2.11b. Steam efficiency
Find thermodynamic efficiency \(\eta=P_{st}/P_{tot}\).

children.text: \[V=\frac43\pi R^3,\quad M=\rho_{Ag}V,\quad N=MN_A/M_{Ag},\quad n=\rho_{Ag}N_A/M_{Ag}.\] The ion charge density is \(en\), electron charge is \(Q=-eN\), and electron mass is \(m_0=m_eN\). Numerically \(V=4.19\times10^{-24}\,\mathrm{m^3}\), \(M=4.39\times10^{-20}\,\mathrm{kg}\), \(N=2.45\times10^5\), \(n=5.85\times10^{28}\,\mathrm{m^{-3}}\), \(en=9.38\times10^9\,\mathrm{C/m^3}\), \(Q=-3.93\times10^{-14}\,\mathrm C\), \(m_0=2.23\times10^{-25}\,\mathrm{kg}\).

Inside a uniform sphere Gauss's law gives \(\mathbf E=\rho\mathbf r/(3\epsilon_0)\). Superpose the displaced negative sphere: \(\mathbf E=\rho[\mathbf r-(\mathbf r-\mathbf x_d)]/(3\epsilon_0)=\rho\mathbf x_d/(3\epsilon_0)\). Thus \(A=1/3\).
The induced inner field is \(enx_p/(3\epsilon_0)\). Multiply by \(-enV\): \[F_x=-\frac{4\pi R^3n^2e^2}{9\epsilon_0}x_p,\qquad W_{el}=\frac{2\pi R^3n^2e^2}{9\epsilon_0}x_p^2.\]
The total internal field vanishes, so \(x_p=3\epsilon_0E_0/(en)\). A cylinder of cross-section \(\pi R^2\) and length \(x_p\) crosses the plane: \(-\Delta Q=-en\pi R^2x_p\).

\[P_{heat}=\frac{m_enV}{2\tau}\langle v^2\rangle,\qquad\langle I^2\rangle=(en\pi R^2)^2\langle v^2\rangle.\] The factor one half in the source's collision model comes from kinetic energy, not from averaging the sinusoid a second time.

At resonance the reactances cancel. With \(R_t=R_{heat}+R_{scat}\), \[\langle I^2\rangle=\frac{8R^2E_0^2}{9R_t^2},\quad P_{heat}=\frac{8R_{heat}R^2E_0^2}{9R_t^2},\quad P_{scat}=\frac{8R_{scat}R^2E_0^2}{9R_t^2}.\]

There are \(n_{np}h^2a=7.3\times10^{11}\) particles, giving \(P_{st}=4.98\,\mathrm{kW}\). Specific steam-production energy is \(c_w(100-20)+L_w=2.59\times10^6\,\mathrm{J/kg}\). The source rounds this to \(2.62\times10^6\) and reports \(\dot m=1.90\times10^{-3}\,\mathrm{kg/s}\). Direct use of the supplied constants gives \(1.92\times10^{-3}\,\mathrm{kg/s}\), also accepted.

solution.text:
Plasmonic Steam Generator
2.1. Particle and electron properties
\[V=\frac43\pi R^3,\quad M=\rho_{Ag}V,\quad N=MN_A/M_{Ag},\quad n=\rho_{Ag}N_A/M_{Ag}.\] The ion charge density is \(en\), electron charge is \(Q=-eN\), and electron mass is \(m_0=m_eN\). Numerically \(V=4.19\times10^{-24}\,\mathrm{m^3}\), \(M=4.39\times10^{-20}\,\mathrm{kg}\), \(N=2.45\times10^5\), \(n=5.85\times10^{28}\,\mathrm{m^{-3}}\), \(en=9.38\times10^9\,\mathrm{C/m^3}\), \(Q=-3.93\times10^{-14}\,\mathrm C\), \(m_0=2.23\times10^{-25}\,\mathrm{kg}\).
2.2. Neutral cavity field
Inside a uniform sphere Gauss's law gives \(\mathbf E=\rho\mathbf r/(3\epsilon_0)\). Superpose the displaced negative sphere: \(\mathbf E=\rho[\mathbf r-(\mathbf r-\mathbf x_d)]/(3\epsilon_0)=\rho\mathbf x_d/(3\epsilon_0)\). Thus \(A=1/3\).
2.3. Restoring force and work
The induced inner field is \(enx_p/(3\epsilon_0)\). Multiply by \(-enV\): \[F_x=-\frac{4\pi R^3n^2e^2}{9\epsilon_0}x_p,\qquad W_{el}=\frac{2\pi R^3n^2e^2}{9\epsilon_0}x_p^2.\]
2.4. Static displacement and separated charge
The total internal field vanishes, so \(x_p=3\epsilon_0E_0/(en)\). A cylinder of cross-section \(\pi R^2\) and length \(x_p\) crosses the plane: \(-\Delta Q=-en\pi R^2x_p\).
2.5a. Equivalent capacitance
Substitution gives \[C=\frac94\pi\epsilon_0R=6.26\times10^{-19}\,\mathrm F.\]
2.5b. Equivalent voltage
\(V_0=\Delta Q/C=4RE_0/3\).
2.6a. Kinetic energy and current
\[W_{kin}=\frac12m_en\frac{4\pi R^3}{3}v^2,\qquad I=-en\pi R^2v.\]
2.6b. Equivalent inductance
\[L=\frac{4m_e}{3\pi Rne^2}=2.57\times10^{-14}\,\mathrm H.\]
2.7a. Plasmon angular frequency
\[\omega_p=(LC)^{-1/2}=\sqrt{\frac{ne^2}{3\epsilon_0m_e}}.\]
2.7b. Resonance values
\(\omega_p=7.88\times10^{15}\,\mathrm{rad/s}\), \(\lambda_p=2\pi c/\omega_p=239\,\mathrm{nm}\).
2.8a. Collision heating
\[P_{heat}=\frac{m_enV}{2\tau}\langle v^2\rangle,\qquad\langle I^2\rangle=(en\pi R^2)^2\langle v^2\rangle.\] The factor one half in the source's collision model comes from kinetic energy, not from averaging the sinusoid a second time.
2.8b. Heating resistance
\[R_{heat}=P_{heat}/\langle I^2\rangle=\frac{2m_e}{3\pi ne^2R\tau}=2.46\,\Omega.\]
2.9. Scattering resistance
Use \(\langle v^2\rangle=\omega_p^2x_0^2/2\) and \(Q=-4\pi enR^3/3\): \[R_{scat}=\frac{8\omega_p^2R^2}{27\pi\epsilon_0c^3}=2.45\,\Omega.\]
2.10a. Resonant absorbed and scattered power
At resonance the reactances cancel. With \(R_t=R_{heat}+R_{scat}\), \[\langle I^2\rangle=\frac{8R^2E_0^2}{9R_t^2},\quad P_{heat}=\frac{8R_{heat}R^2E_0^2}{9R_t^2},\quad P_{scat}=\frac{8R_{scat}R^2E_0^2}{9R_t^2}.\]
2.10b. Illumination values
\(E_0=\sqrt{2S/(\epsilon_0c)}=27.4\,\mathrm{kV/m}\), \(P_{heat}=6.82\,\mathrm{nW}\), and \(P_{scat}=6.81\,\mathrm{nW}\).
2.11a. Steam mass rate
There are \(n_{np}h^2a=7.3\times10^{11}\) particles, giving \(P_{st}=4.98\,\mathrm{kW}\). Specific steam-production energy is \(c_w(100-20)+L_w=2.59\times10^6\,\mathrm{J/kg}\). The source rounds this to \(2.62\times10^6\) and reports \(\dot m=1.90\times10^{-3}\,\mathrm{kg/s}\). Direct use of the supplied constants gives \(1.92\times10^{-3}\,\mathrm{kg/s}\), also accepted.
2.11b. Steam efficiency
The incident power is \(h^2S=10.0\,\mathrm{kW}\). Hence \(\eta=4.98/10.0=0.498\).
